thread:
priya: quick RFC follow-up 1: thinking about a 'gradient canary' approach that treats traffic fraction as a continuous function f(t) and lets the runtime do low-cost, deterministic routing. jotting tradeoffs and a minimal policy sketch.
jason: love the idea. two quick flags: 1) session affinity, 2) runtime decision cost for streaming.
priya: agreed. propose two affinity strategies: 'sticky-hash' (hash(session_id) < f(t) -> stable variant without extra state) and 'drain-next' (pin until next request). policy chooses affinity_mode.
maria: health signals we should evaluate: err_rate_pct, latency_p95_ms, cpu_util_pct, and optional quality_delta when eval hooks exist. need an aggregation contract.
lia: composite health score sounds right. example: S = 0.6*err_norm + 0.3*p95_norm + 0.1*quality_drop_norm. weights configurable per route.
priya: controller responsibilities: emit target_frac and smoothing_window_s (max df/dt); evaluate telemetry windows; decide state transitions. runtime responsibilities: enforce routing cheaply, stream aggregated telemetry back.
jason: implementation sketch: use deterministic hashing with epoch to allow controlled remapping. pseudo: 
```
# per-request (or per-session) decision
if hash(session_id, epoch)/MAX < target_frac:
  route -> canary
else:
  route -> baseline
```
Caching decision at session start for streaming avoids per-chunk cost.
maria: abort logic: sliding windows + require M consecutive windows where composite S > abort_threshold before auto-rollback. add cooldown and hysteresis to avoid oscillation.
opsbot: [bot] canary run 1769989000 summary: peak_frac=0.13, p95_delta=+10ms, err_delta=0.4% -> https://deployments/redwood/1769989000
jason: 10ms p95 bump might be fine on some routes, not on others. add route_profile that tightens thresholds for high-sla paths.
priya: policy surface (minimal): route, variant, baseline, target_frac, smoothing_window_s, affinity_mode, weights, abort_thresholds, min_hold_s, cooldown_s, fallback_variant, run_id. controller <-> runtime via signed pushes; telemetry batched every window.
lia: Console UX: fraction slider with "pace" presets (fast/steady/slow) mapping to smoothing_window_s; timeline overlays f(t) and S(t); quick actions to pause auto-rollback.
maria: ops playbook: auto-rollback should open a Slack thread with S(t) snapshot, random failing prompts, and a single-click "pause auto" + link to runbook. include rollback reason code.
priya: edge-case: fallback to a quantized cheaper variant with different quality curve. policy should expose fallback_variant and reason taxonomy so Console shows cost/quality tradeoffs.
jason: telemetry format recommendation: per-window aggregate: {window_start, window_end, variant, requests, errs, p50,p95,p99}. keep it compact and signed.
lia: security: policy payloads must be signed (ed25519) for Dedicated/Private; runtime verifies issuer ACL before applying. telemetry can be aggregated locally before export.
priya: open questions: 1) default weights per route-class? 2) limits on concurrent canaries per runtime to bound memory/CPU? 3) sampling for low-traffic routes (need reservoir sampling or synthetic traffic?).
maria: I'll draft a short runbook snippet for ops and a list of route_profile defaults. jason: will prototype a small proto for policy + telemetry. lia: will mock Console wireframes.
priya: thanks all 1. I'll fold this into the RFC addendum. tagging eng-runtime and eng-platform for review. end thread.
